content.text:
Silhouette: Four-legged tortoise frame. Host frame: the tortoise sets the outline, body size and overall frame. A single creature combining a tortoise and a domestic goat. The head is that of the tortoise, fully visible and uncluttered, with clear, discernible eyes. Details: tortoise body and legs with its own hard shell plates on the face, neck, shoulders, belly, hips, legs and tail; plain coat with no stripes or spots. From the domestic goat, as parts and materials on the tortoise's own body, dense fur in its own colors grown from the skin as the tortoise's own covering over the back and flanks; it replaces the tortoise's hard shell plates there and conforms to the tortoise's body, sized to the tortoise's body and following its contours. The hard shell plates stop at the covering's edge, while the face, neck, shoulders, belly, hips, legs and tail retain the tortoise's own hard shell plates. The covering follows the body's own shape. Bilaterally symmetrical, with recognizable limbs and visible sense organs. Habitat cue (grassland): dark back and light belly (strong countershading). Prosaic detail: natural lighting, feet in firm contact with the ground with a soft shadow, normal wear on hooves, claws and skin. One creature, full body, side three-quarter view, plain light background, natural history illustration.
Aspect ratio: 1:1.

summary.text:
**Designing hybrid creature illustration**
I'm planning a natural history illustration of a single hybrid with a tortoise frame and goat fur, keeping the tortoise head fully visible with clear eyes and a plain, unpatterned coat.
**Drafting natural history illustration**
I'm planning a side three-quarter natural history plate of a tortoise with dense goat fur covering the back and flanks, while the face, neck, limbs, belly and tail keep shell plates, with dark back and light belly countershading on a plain light background.
**Refining goat illustration details**
I'm planning another generation to emphasize clearer goat features, adding more fur texture and visible legs while keeping the current version as a solid base.
